chapters.title: Large numbers and place-value clues
chapters.tagline: Read seven- and eight-digit values and justify comparison or rounding.
outcomes: I can build and compare large numbers.
I can round and solve digit clues.
I can use Roman numerals.

vocab.meaning: What a digit is worth because of its place. In 3,52,07,184 the 3 is worth 3 crore.
One lakh is 1,00,000. It has 6 digits.
One crore is 1,00,00,000. It has 8 digits.
Changing a number to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand.

see.title: Eight places
text: An eight-digit number has crores, ten lakhs, lakhs, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
In 35,207,184 the first digit 3 is worth thirty million.
In the Indian system it is written 3,52,07,184.

see.title: Read and name big numbers
text: Group the digits from the right: 3 crore, 52 lakh, 07 thousand and 184.
Say it: three crore, fifty-two lakh, seven thousand, one hundred eighty-four.
A zero keeps a place, but we do not say it.

c.caption: Three crore fifty-two lakh seven thousand one hundred eighty-four

see.title: Compare and order
text: More digits means a bigger number.
If the digits are equal in number, compare from the left.
Order 18,194, 34,238 and 83,119 from least to greatest.

see.title: Round to the nearest ten
text: Look at the ones digit. 5 or more rounds up. 4 or fewer rounds down.
245 is halfway between 240 and 250.
We round halfway numbers up, so 245 rounds to 250.

see.title: Roman numerals
text: C is 100, L is 50, X is 10, V is 5 and I is 1. D is 500.
Write the biggest parts first: 478 is 400 + 70 + 8.
That is CD, LXX and VIII: CDLXXVIII.

try.prompt: Build 24,05,000: 24 lakh 5 thousand. Then switch to international commas and read it again.
try.success: 24,05,000 is 24 lakh 5 thousand. With international commas it is 2,405,000.
try.hint: Add 2 to Ten lakhs, 4 to Lakhs and 5 to Thousands. Leave the other columns at 0.

try.prompt: Round 347 to the nearest ten. Move the marker to the answer.
try.hint: The ones digit is 7. Round up.

try.prompt: Use each card once to make the smallest number. Tap a gap, then a card.
try.hint: Put the smallest digit in the biggest place.

try.prompt: Write 49 in Roman numerals. Tap each gap, then a tile.
try.success: XL is 40 and IX is 9, so XLIX is 49.

chapters.title: Solve stories with factors and multiples
chapters.tagline: Choose a method, use exact groups or repeating schedules, and check the result.
outcomes: I can solve a linked calculation story.
I can find common factors and multiples.
I can use a repeating schedule and interpret leftovers.

vocab.meaning: A number that divides another number exactly.
A number in a times table. 12, 24 and 36 are multiples of 12.
The highest common factor. It is the biggest factor two numbers share.
The lowest common multiple. It is the smallest number both can reach.

see.title: Bar models for stories
text: Draw one bar for the total and split it into parts.
A convoy carries 9100 crates. 6200 are water tanks.
The rest are food pods: 9100 − 6200 = 2900.

see.title: Common factors
text: List the factors of each number, then circle the ones that match.
Common factors are 1, 2, 3 and 6. The HCF is 6.

see.title: Meet again
text: A drone docks every 3 minutes. A scout docks every 4 minutes.
List the multiples of each: 3, 6, 9, 12 and 4, 8, 12.
They first dock together at 12. That is the LCM.

see.title: Leftovers
text: 32 packs go into crates of 3. That makes 10 full crates.
10 × 3 = 30, so 2 packs are left over.

try.prompt: A drone docks every 4 minutes and a scout every 6. Hop in 4s to the first time both dock.
try.success: 12 is the first multiple of both 4 and 6.
try.hint: Use the hop button, then check 12 is in the 6 times table.

try.prompt: Show 12 as 2 rows of 6. The 6 is a common factor of 12 and 18.
try.hint: Make 2 rows with 6 in each row.

try.prompt: 32 packs. 10 crates of 3 hold 30. Add the left-over packs to level the balance.

chapters.title: Fractions, mixed numbers and what is left
chapters.tagline: Connect pictures and quantities before solving repeated changes.
outcomes: I can match equivalent and mixed fractions.
I can order fractions and find a fraction of an amount.
I can find what is left after fraction changes.

vocab.meaning: A whole number and a fraction together, like 1 4/5.
A fraction where the top is bigger than the bottom, like 9/5.
Having the same value, like 5/7 and 10/14.

see.title: Mixed numbers
text: Each strip has 5 equal parts. One strip is full, the next has 4 shaded.
That is 1 whole and 4/5, written 1 4/5.
Count all the shaded parts: 9 fifths, so 1 4/5 = 9/5.

see.title: Equivalent fractions
text: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
The shaded amount stays the same.

see.title: Put fractions in order
text: Give the fractions the same bottom number.
Now the order is easy: 2/3, then 3/4, then 5/6.

see.title: A fraction of an amount
text: To find 2/6 of 96, split 96 into 6 equal parts.
Each part is 96 ÷ 6 = 16.
2 parts make 32. So 2/6 of 96 is 32.

see.title: What is left after changes
text: A base has 42 crates. 1/6 are used, which is 7. That leaves 35.
Next 3/5 of the 35 are used, which is 21.
35 − 21 = 14 crates are left.

try.prompt: Shade the 14-part bar so it shows the same amount as 5/7.
Shade 5/6 of this 12-part bar.
18 counters make 6 equal groups. Show 6 groups of 3. Each group is 1/6.

chapters.title: Tenths, hundredths and decimal calculations
chapters.tagline: Connect fractions and place value, then line up decimal places.
outcomes: I can show decimals on a grid or line.
I can compare decimals and link them to fractions.
I can calculate decimal money and measures.

vocab.meaning: One of ten equal parts. 0.1 is one tenth.
One of one hundred equal parts. 0.01 is one hundredth.
The dot that separates whole numbers from parts of a whole.

see.title: Tenths
text: Cut one whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth, 0.1.
3 tenths is 3/10, written 0.3.
The 3 sits in the tenths place.

see.title: Hundredths on a grid
text: A hundred-grid has 100 equal squares. Each is 0.01.
37 squares shaded is 37/100, or 0.37.
That is 3 tenths and 7 hundredths.

see.title: Tenths on a bar
text: Think of a bar split into 10 equal parts.
4 parts shaded is 0.4 or 4/10.
4/10 is the same as 2/5.

see.title: Line up the decimal points
text: When you add decimals, line up the points so tenths sit under tenths.
Add Rs 7.44 and Rs 26.56.
The total is Rs 34.00.

see.title: Compare decimals
text: Write both with the same number of places. 0.6 is 0.60.
Compare 60 hundredths with 45 hundredths.
0.6 is bigger than 0.45.

try.prompt: Shade 0.7 of the 10 squares.
Shade 0.6 of the bar.
Put the decimals in order from least to greatest. Tap a gap, then a tile.

chapters.title: Angles, symmetry, perimeter and area
chapters.tagline: Name the measurement needed before using shape facts.
outcomes: I can find a perimeter or area.
I can use angle facts.
I can complete symmetry or fold a cube net.

vocab.meaning: The turn between two lines that meet. We measure it in degrees.
The distance all the way round a shape.
The space inside a shape, in square units.
A mirror line that makes two matching halves.

see.title: Angles on a line
text: A straight line makes an angle of 180 degrees.
If one angle is 76 degrees, the other is 180 − 76.
The other angle is 104 degrees.

see.title: Perimeter and a missing side
text: A rectangle has a perimeter of 42 m and one side of 9 m.
Two sides of 9 m use 18 m. 42 − 18 = 24 m for the other two sides.
Each of those sides is 12 m.

see.title: Area of a step shape
text: Split the shape into rectangles, or take a corner away.
A 6 by 6 square with a 2 by 2 corner removed has 36 − 4 = 32 squares.
Its area is 32 square units.

c.caption: A 6 by 6 square with a 2 by 2 corner missing.

see.title: Symmetry
text: Fold along the mirror line. Matching squares land on top of each other.
Count how many squares are on each side.
The mirror makes a twin for every shaded square.

see.title: Fold a cube net
text: A cube net has 6 squares joined along edges.
When it folds, squares in a row of 3 make faces that face each other.
The first and third squares in a row end up opposite.

try.prompt: Make an obtuse angle of 135°. Drag the arm, or use the arrow keys.
try.success: 135° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.
try.hint: A right angle is 90°. Open the arm 45° more. Shift with an arrow key moves 15°.

try.prompt: Look at this angle. Is it acute, right, obtuse, straight or a full turn?
try.success: The arm is past the square corner but short of the straight line, so it is obtuse.
try.hint: Compare it with 90° (a square corner) and 180° (a straight line).

try.prompt: Shade a rectangle with area 16 and perimeter 20.
Shade 5 squares on the left. The mirror shades the twins. Make 10 shaded squares.
try.hint: Tap 5 different squares on the left.

chapters.title: Convert and compare measurements
chapters.tagline: Read scales and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.
outcomes: I can read a dial or thermometer.
I can compare mixed units.
I can solve a measurement story and estimate sensibly.

vocab.meaning: Change a measurement to another unit with the same size.
How much a container holds.
A sensible guess close to the real measurement.

see.title: Read a dial
text: Check what each small mark is worth before you read.
This gauge goes from 0 to 20 kg. The needle is on 14.
The mass is 14 kg.

see.title: Convert units
text: To change a big unit to a small unit, multiply by 1000.

see.title: Compare in the same unit
text: Which is greater: 18 l or 17,184 ml?
18,000 is more than 17,184, so 18 l is greater.

c.caption: 18 l (18,000 ml) is heavier than 17,184 ml.

see.title: Choose a sensible unit
text: Small, light things use grams. Bigger things use kilograms.
A pencil is a few grams.
A school bag is a few kilograms.

try.prompt: Sort each item by the unit that fits best. Tap an item, then a box.
try.success: Light things use grams. Heavier things use kilograms.
try.hint: Would you weigh it in your hand or on a big scale?

try.prompt: The right pan holds 10 kg. The left pan holds 4 kg. Add blocks until it is level.

chapters.title: Elapsed time, timetables and dates
chapters.tagline: Separate actual time, displayed time and calendar intervals.
outcomes: I can find elapsed time.
I can correct clock errors and switch time formats.
I can use a calendar and timetable.

vocab.meaning: How much time has passed from the start to the end.
A way of telling time that counts from 00:00 to 23:59.
A clock that shows an earlier time than the true time.

see.title: Elapsed time
text: A drone leaves at 6:30 a.m. and arrives at 10:50 a.m.
6:30 to 10:30 is 4 hours. 10:30 to 10:50 is 20 minutes.
The trip takes 4 hours 20 minutes.

see.title: The 24-hour clock
text: After 12:00 noon the 24-hour clock keeps counting: 13:00, 14:00 and so on.
To change 14:15 to 12-hour time, take away 12.

see.title: Slow clocks
text: A slow clock shows too little time, so add the gap.
This clock shows 3:00 and is 45 minutes slow.
The true time is 3:45.

c.caption: Shows 3:00, but it is 45 minutes slow.

see.title: Dates and days
text: A week has 7 days. Add 7 to a date and you get the same weekday.
In March 2026 the 1st is a Sunday.
So the 12th is a Thursday.

try.prompt: A mission log says 14:15. Show that time on the 12-hour clock.
This clock shows 3:00 but is 45 minutes slow. Set the true time.
March 2026 starts on a Sunday. Tap the second Thursday.
try.hint: The first Thursday is the 5th. Add 7.

chapters.title: Plan a budget and compare value
chapters.tagline: Compare like quantities and account for every price change.
outcomes: I can total purchases and find missing prices.
I can compare value for money.
I can check a budget after a discount.

vocab.meaning: The most money you plan to spend.
An amount taken off the price.
The lowest price for one item or one unit.
A paper that lists what you bought and what you paid.

see.title: Add the purchases
text: Add the prices on the board for the items you choose.
Rs 50 + Rs 20 + Rs 20 = Rs 90.
Check your total against the budget.

see.title: Find a missing price
text: The receipt total is Rs 250. Two items cost Rs 150 together.
The missing price is 250 − 150 = Rs 100.
Draw a bar model if it helps.

see.title: Compare value
text: Pack A: 2 crates for Rs 36 is Rs 18 each.
Pack B: 3 crates for Rs 30 is Rs 10 each.
Pack B is the better value.

see.title: Discounts
text: 25% is one quarter.
A module costs Rs 600. A quarter of 600 is Rs 150.
The sale price is 600 − 150 = Rs 450.

try.prompt: A Rs 120 item has 25% off. The sale price is Rs 90. Pay Rs 90 using exactly 3 notes.
25% means 1 part in 4. Shade the discount part.

chapters.title: Charts, averages and true statements
chapters.tagline: Read the scale, combine results and justify a claim.
outcomes: I can read pictographs and scaled bars.
I can compare two displays or a line graph.
I can find an average and check a chart statement.

vocab.meaning: The note that tells you what each symbol or step stands for.
How much each step on an axis is worth.
The average. Add all the values, then divide by how many there are.
A graph that joins points to show change over time.

see.title: Pictograph keys
text: Read the key first. Here each ● is 5 crates.
Count the symbols, then multiply by 5.
Four symbols mean 20 crates.

see.title: Unusual scales
text: Check the numbers up the side before you read a bar.
If each gridline is 20, a bar halfway between 40 and 60 is 50.
Never assume the scale counts by 1.

see.title: The mean
text: Four outposts collected 12, 14, 10 and 16 samples.
Total: 12 + 14 + 10 + 16 = 52. Divide by 4.
The mean is 13. If every outpost had the same, each would have 13.

see.title: Check a statement
text: Read the claim. Then test it with the bars.
Find each value and compare it to the claim.
A claim is true only if the numbers match every time.

try.prompt: The mean is 13. Change each bar so that all four bars show 13.
try.success: Each bar is the mean, 13. The total is still 52.
try.hint: Take from the tall bars and add to the short ones.

try.prompt: Each ● is 5 crates. Show 35 crates for Outpost B.
try.hint: 35 divided by 5 is how many symbols?

chapters.title: Codes, reflections and logic puzzles
chapters.tagline: Test every clue and distinguish turning, mirroring and flipping.
outcomes: I can use codes, series and ranking clues.
I can follow directions and count combinations.
I can reason about mirror clocks and reflected words.
I can order words by their logical meaning and find an exact embedded figure.

vocab.meaning: A list of letters or numbers that follows a rule.
The flipped copy you see in a mirror.
One choice from each group put together.

see.title: Letter series
text: Look at each part of the pair separately.
In DZ, EY, FX, GW the first letters move forward and the second letters move back.
The next pair is HV.

c.caption: First letter forward, second letter back

see.title: Mirror images
text: A mirror at the side flips left and right.
The order of the letters turns around, and each letter is flipped.
Test it with a small mirror at home.

see.title: Count the combinations
text: 7 flag colours and 6 flag symbols make 7 × 6 = 42 combinations.
Each colour pairs with every symbol.
An array shows the pairs in rows and columns.

see.title: Turns and directions
text: A rover faces east, moves forward 2, turns left and moves forward 2.
Left from east is north.
Draw the path before you decide where it ends.

see.title: Mirror clocks
text: At 1:30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 1 and 2.
The angle between them is 135 degrees.
Check every hand, not only the minute hand.

try.prompt: Guide the rover to the flag. Go forward twice, turn left, then forward twice.
try.success: Two forward, left, two forward reaches the flag.
try.hint: Forward, forward, turn left, forward, forward.

try.prompt: 4 colours and 3 symbols. Build the array of all combinations.
Series: D, E, F, ?  What is the next first letter? Tap the gap, then a tile.
try.success: D, E, F, G: the letters go forward by 1.
